# ThePrototype Docs

> User documentation for ThePrototype (https://theprototype.app), a collaborative 3D prototyping app that runs in the browser: peer-to-peer sessions with no account, a visual node graph for behaviour, games, VR and AI tools. Each link is the page's Markdown; images and short video loops are described in words.

Every page in one file: https://docs.theprototype.app/llms-full.txt

## Getting Started

- [Welcome](https://docs.theprototype.app/index.md): ThePrototype is a collaborative 3D prototyping app that runs in your browser — sessions are peer-to-peer, and you need no account.
- [Controls](https://docs.theprototype.app/controls.md): How to move the camera, select and transform objects, and find every keyboard shortcut — on desktop and in VR.
- [The Interface](https://docs.theprototype.app/interface.md): Since 1.30 every window, menu, dialog, the main HUD and the phone layout are built from one small kit of parts and one set of colours. This page is the map: where things are and what the shapes…
- [Touch Controls](https://docs.theprototype.app/touch-controls.md): On a phone or tablet, Play shows a move stick on the left, a look drag on the right and the game's own action buttons — Jump, Throw, Grab, Use… — exactly the actions the game needs. Every control…
- [Tours](https://docs.theprototype.app/tours.md): Short first-run tours show you around: Welcome to ThePrototype VR mode in the headset, and the editor tour on a screen. Every tour has Skip, Back, Next and Don't show again. A tour you leave…
- [Units](https://docs.theprototype.app/units.md): The scene is metres and radians underneath, always. Units change how numbers are shown to you and typed by you — nothing else. That makes them a local preference: you can work in inches while a…
- [Themes & Appearance](https://docs.theprototype.app/appearance.md): How the app's own interface looks is a choice for this device only — your theme is never sent to anyone, and the 3D viewport keeps following the scene's environment (sky, background, grid),…
- [Accessibility](https://docs.theprototype.app/accessibility.md): Most of it lives in Settings ▸ Accessibility (under General, right after Interface). Settings search finds the page by accessibility, a11y, zoom, low vision, contrast, colour blind, motion,…
- [Settings](https://docs.theprototype.app/settings.md): Since 1.35 Settings opens beside your work: an open sidebar, the docked windows and the Node editor stay where they are on a computer and an unfolded phone. On a folded phone Settings is a…
- [Tools & connections](https://docs.theprototype.app/tools-and-connections.md): Each tool is one row:
- [Privacy & Error Reports](https://docs.theprototype.app/privacy.md): In a session your scene goes from your browser straight to the people you connect to (peer-to-peer); our servers introduce you, relay the encrypted traffic when a direct link is impossible, and…
- [Security & Self-hosting](https://docs.theprototype.app/security.md): theprototype.app lets people share scenes that carry code: Script nodes, Behaviour files, a Character Controller's Player code and Custom (code) HUD elements. This page says where that code runs,…
- [Your Character](https://docs.theprototype.app/avatars.md): Since 1.24 everyone in a session appears as a rigged, animated character instead of a floating head. The body stands under the person's viewpoint, walks, runs, strafes, jumps and idles with the…
- [Connection](https://docs.theprototype.app/connection.md): How peers find each other, how to invite someone into your scene, and how to point the app at a signaling server you trust.
- [Invite People and Agents](https://docs.theprototype.app/invites.md): An invite link lets someone into your session without an approval card: a friend you send it to, or an AI agent you paste it into. You decide what it allows — View or Edit, how long it lasts and…
- [Users & Moderation](https://docs.theprototype.app/people.md): Everyone in your session is listed in the Connected panel (the people button, top right). Each person has a menu: find them, look at their character, mute or hide them for yourself — and, if you…
- [Sharing into the App](https://docs.theprototype.app/sharing-into-the-app.md): On Android, Share a file from the gallery, the file manager or another app and pick theprototype:

## Building

- [Explorer](https://docs.theprototype.app/explorer.md): The Explorer is the session's file library — import files, organize them into folders, preview them, share them with the people you are connected to, and drag them straight into the scene.
- [Importing Big Models](https://docs.theprototype.app/import-optimize.md): When you import a model with more than 50,000 triangles or a texture larger than 2048 px:
- [Edit in Blender](https://docs.theprototype.app/edit-in-blender.md): Take a model to Blender (or Maya, 3ds Max, Cascadeur, any tool that reads and writes glTF) and bring it back. The object keeps its place, flows, physics and clips. There is nothing to install.
- [Free Assets (CC0)](https://docs.theprototype.app/free-assets.md): The Asset Browser (1.38) brings free, public-domain (CC0) assets straight into your project: models, skies (HDRIs) and texture sets from Poly Haven, and PBR materials from ambientCG. No account,…
- [Packs](https://docs.theprototype.app/packs.md): Packs are shareable bundles of 3D assets that appear in the Explorer's Packs section — browse them like folders and place their items like any import.
- [Levels of Detail](https://docs.theprototype.app/lod.md): A level of detail is a simpler version of a model that draws instead of the full one when the model is small on screen. Far-away objects then cost a fraction of their triangles — which is what…
- [Prefabs](https://docs.theprototype.app/prefabs.md): Prefabs are objects (or whole groups) you save once and reuse anywhere — your personal building blocks.
- [Material Presets](https://docs.theprototype.app/materials.md): A material preset is a named look for an object's surface — colour, roughness, metalness, glow, transparency and up to two image maps (a texture and a normal map) — that you apply with one click.…
- [Architecture](https://docs.theprototype.app/architecture.md): Since 1.27 you can build rooms and houses from parametric pieces: walls with doorways and window openings, doors and windows that open, and four kinds of stairs. Every piece is a set of numbers…
- [Mesh Editing](https://docs.theprototype.app/mesh-editing.md): Reshape any mesh by hand: drag its vertices, slide its edges, extrude and bevel its faces, fill holes, give a surface thickness, cut it with a knife, mirror one half onto the other — or combine…
- [Splines](https://docs.theprototype.app/splines.md): Click out a path and get a solid tube that follows it — a road, a pipe, a cable, a river bed, a handrail. Splines stay editable forever: every one carries the points you placed, so you (or any…
- [Snapping](https://docs.theprototype.app/snapping.md): Snapping makes things line up without you nudging them into place. There are two kinds, and they work together: a grid that quantises how far a drag moves, and element snapping that lands the…
- [Measure, Align & Distribute](https://docs.theprototype.app/measure-align.md): Since 1.38 the Measure tool snaps to the geometry and chains segments, and a selection can be lined up, spaced out and dropped onto the ground in one click. Since 1.39 the measurements you keep…
- [Reference Images](https://docs.theprototype.app/reference-images.md)
- [UV & Textures](https://docs.theprototype.app/uv-editor.md): A texture is a flat image wrapped around a 3D model. The UV editor shows you that wrapping — the model's surface unfolded into a square — and lets you rearrange it, generate it from scratch, paint…
- [Image Editor](https://docs.theprototype.app/image-editor.md): New in 1.32: the Image editor crops, rotates, flips, resizes and adjusts a picture in your Explorer library. When you save, every texture made from that picture updates for everyone in the session.
- [Shader Graph](https://docs.theprototype.app/shader-graph.md): Build a material out of nodes instead of sliders. A shader graph replaces what a material looks like — its colour, glow, roughness, surface detail, transparency, even where its vertices sit — and…
- [Shader Nodes](https://docs.theprototype.app/shader-nodes.md): Every node the Shader editor offers, grouped exactly as the palette and the right-click menu group them. Each node's one-line description is the same text the editor shows in its info pane when…
- [Scene Look (Post-processing)](https://docs.theprototype.app/post-processing.md): Grade the finished frame. A scene look is a stack of screen-space effects — ambient occlusion, colour grading, bloom, vignette, film grain, pixelation — applied over the whole viewport after the…
- [Animation](https://docs.theprototype.app/animation.md): Give any object a clip: a named animation made of keyframes. Open a door, run a lift, spin a turntable, blink a light. Clips are stored with the object, replicate to everyone in the session, play…
- [Characters and motion](https://docs.theprototype.app/characters-and-motion.md): Any rigged model is a character, any clip plays on any humanoid, and the clips are small files of their own. Characters and motions come as free CC0 packs, and a character downloads with its clips…
- [Timeline (Cutscenes)](https://docs.theprototype.app/timeline.md): Sequences are part of the scene: they are saved with it, shared live with everyone in the session (late joiners too), undoable, and they play in exported and published games.
- [Physics & Simulation](https://docs.theprototype.app/physics.md): Drop, stack, collide, weld and throw. ThePrototype has a real-time rigid-body simulation (Rapier) you can start at any moment — objects fall, pile up and knock each other over, and everyone in the…
- [Colliders](https://docs.theprototype.app/colliders.md): Physics never collides your triangles. It collides a simple stand-in — a collider — that is fast to test and forgiving: a box, a sphere, a capsule, a convex skin, a handful of convex pieces you…
- [Particle Effects](https://docs.theprototype.app/particles.md): Add dust, smoke, fire, sparkles, confetti and sparks to your scene. Emitters attach to any object (or stand on their own), follow it around, and — because everything replicates — everyone in the…
- [Water](https://docs.theprototype.app/water.md): Any object can be water: a tank, a pool, a lake, an ocean, a pit of lava. Water has waves, see-through refraction, light patterns (caustics) on the floor, foam on the wave crests and along the…
- [Fluid Tank & Jiggle](https://docs.theprototype.app/simulation.md): Two kinds of motion that are about the look more than the rules: a fluid tank of particle liquid you can slosh, pour and drain, and the Jiggle node, which makes any object lag, wobble and sway.…
- [Fluids: Emitters & Flow Paths](https://docs.theprototype.app/fluids.md): Since 1.25 you can pour real particle water into the open scene: it pools, splashes, lands on meshes and joins any water it is poured into. Flow paths carry it along rivers, chutes and pipes, and…
- [Terrain & Sculpting](https://docs.theprototype.app/terrain.md): Add ground and shape it two ways: procedurally, by dialling in hills from a handful of numbers, and by hand, with a brush that raises, lowers, smooths and flattens. Every edit replicates to your…
- [Scatter](https://docs.theprototype.app/scatter.md): A scatter set is its settings + a seed + your hand edits. Every computer in your session builds the same instances from those, and so does every reload — a set of thousands of instances travels as…
- [Saving & Sessions](https://docs.theprototype.app/saving.md): How to save and load your work: the recommended .tpscene bundle, the whole-project .tp, GLTF interchange, named sessions, and autosave.
- [Checkpoints](https://docs.theprototype.app/checkpoints.md): A checkpoint is a copy of the scene as it is right now — objects, node graphs, HUD, sky, physics, the camera — kept on this device, with a name, an optional note, a picture and a time. Autosave…
- [Loading Placeholders](https://docs.theprototype.app/loading.md): When you open a level built from kit pieces (Castle Courtyard, the Tavern, …) — or a peer sends you one — each piece first appears as a placeholder box where it will stand, and the real model…
- [Projects](https://docs.theprototype.app/projects.md): A project is everything in your Explorer: the library items and folders, every saved scene with its version history, and the project's name. It lives on your machine (IndexedDB) and replicates to…

## Viewport

- [Camera & View](https://docs.theprototype.app/camera.md): Everything about how the scene looks on your screen — the camera lens, render mode, shadows, the grid and the environment — lives in one place: Configure Scene.
- [Recording a Video](https://docs.theprototype.app/recording.md): Record a short video of the viewport while the recorder drives the camera: a turntable round your model, or a flythrough of your saved views. The result is a .webm file in your Explorer, ready to…
- [Notifications & Notes](https://docs.theprototype.app/notifications.md): The top-right cluster next to your avatar holds two history surfaces — the notification center and the scene-notes drawer — plus the tools for leaving notes on objects, chatting and pinging things…
- [Performance & Budgets](https://docs.theprototype.app/performance.md): How big a scene can get, how to see where it stands, and what the app does on its own when a scene is more than your machine can draw.
- [Profiler & Recordings](https://docs.theprototype.app/profiler.md): The Statistics window tells you where a scene stands right now. The Profiler tells you what happened: it records frame time, draw calls, triangles and the quality level over time, and — in a…

## Flow Graph

- [Node System](https://docs.theprototype.app/node-system.md): The Flow editor is a visual node graph that drives scene behavior — animation, logic, interactivity and sound — replicated live to every peer.
- [Main Graph & Node Properties](https://docs.theprototype.app/main-graph.md): A scene's flow graph is now called Main. It is where a game's logic starts: what the game does, which code runs it and how the pieces are wired are all reachable from here. Every node on it lists…
- [Node Editor: Keyboard, Groups & Notes](https://docs.theprototype.app/node-editor.md): Since 1.23 the node editor has its own keyboard: shortcuts go to the panel you are working in, so the same letter can mean one thing among the nodes and another in the 3D view. Nodes can be…
- [Node Graph Debugger](https://docs.theprototype.app/debugger.md): It is yours alone. The other players in the session keep playing, and nothing you set in the debugger is saved into the scene or sent to anyone.
- [Code Workspace](https://docs.theprototype.app/code-workspace.md): The code workspace is one place for every piece of code in a scene: a Script node's code, a behaviour, a .js script file from your Library, a module's own source (read-only), and the flow graph…
- [Flow Nodes](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes.md): Every node the Flow editor offers, grouped exactly as the palette groups them. Each node's one-line description is the same text the editor shows in its info pane (and the palette's tooltip) when…
- [Object Flows](https://docs.theprototype.app/object-flows.md): Every object can now carry its own node graph, alongside the shared Scene flow. Object flows keep behavior with the thing it belongs to — a door knows how to open, a lamp knows how to flicker —…
- [Nodes › Input › Slider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/slider.md): An interactive slider that outputs a number — the quickest way to hand-tune any numeric input live.
- [Nodes › Input › Color Picker](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/colorpicker.md): Outputs a color chosen with a swatch — the color source for anything that paints.
- [Nodes › Input › Switcher](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/switcher.md): A radio-button list that outputs the index of the selected item — a hand-operated multi-way switch. Since 1.27 it is also a multi-way switch for values: each item has its own input, and the value…
- [Nodes › Input › Number](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/number.md): A constant numeric value — the simplest source node.
- [Nodes › Input › Vector3](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/vector3.md): An x/y/z triple — used as a direction, an offset, or most often a fixed point in the world.
- [Nodes › Input › Toggle](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/toggle.md): A checkbox that outputs true or false — a hand-operated on/off switch.
- [Nodes › Input › Random](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/random.md): A random number in a range — deterministic, so every peer sees the same "random" value.
- [Nodes › Input › Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/time.md): The synced clock as a value — the heartbeat behind almost every animation recipe.
- [Nodes › Scene › Object Selector](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectselector.md): Binds the graph to a scene object — the sink every effect must reach, and an object reference for sensor nodes.
- [Nodes › Scene › Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/velocity.md): Outputs how fast the connected object is moving right now, in metres per second.
- [Nodes › Scene › Measure](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/measure.md): Reads a number off an object: how tall it is, where its top is, how fast it is going.
- [Nodes › Scene › Spawn](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spawn.md): Makes copies of an object while the simulation runs — crates off a conveyor, targets, debris, ammo, waves of anything.
- [Nodes › Object Flow › Flow Input](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowinput.md): Declares a public input socket for an object flow — the way the Scene flow feeds a value into an object's own graph.
- [Nodes › Object Flow › Flow Output](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowoutput.md): Declares a public output socket for an object flow — the way an object publishes a value back to the Scene flow.
- [Nodes › Object Flow › Object Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/objectflow.md): Embeds an object's own graph into the Scene flow as a single card — the way to compose object flows into a bigger machine without opening each one.
- [Nodes › Game › Set Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setgamestate.md): Switches the shared game state — menu, playing, paused or over — when a pulse arrives. Every player follows the same state: it is the one switch a Start, Pause or Game Over button writes to.
- [Nodes › Game › On Game State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongamestate.md): Fires a pulse when the shared game state becomes the one you pick — the hook for "when the round starts" or "when the game is over". With edge exit it fires when the game leaves that state instead.
- [Nodes › Game › Set Active Camera](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcamera.md): Makes a camera object the active view for every player when a pulse arrives.
- [Nodes › Game › Camera Rig](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/camerarig.md): Moves a scene camera object so it follows a target, looks at it, or both — a chase camera behind a car, a camera that keeps a player in frame. New in 1.27; find it in the palette under Game.
- [Nodes › Game › Set Look](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setlook.md): Switches a camera's look — its post-processing — on or off when a pulse arrives, and by default also looks through that camera.
- [Nodes › Game › Game Start](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamestart.md): Fires once when the game starts (Play, or a round reset) - the place to spawn, reset counters and arm timers.
- [Nodes › Game › Travel to scene](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/travel.md): Loads another saved scene by name when a pulse arrives - a door to the next level, replicated to everyone.
- [Nodes › Game › All Players](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/allplayers.md): Fires a pulse once every player in Play answers yes to a condition — the group gate that makes sure nobody is left behind ("everyone is at the portal", "everyone has three laps").
- [Nodes › Game › Set Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvariable.md): Writes a named number when a pulse arrives — a score, lives, a difficulty. With scope shared it is one number the whole game shares, with no object needed to hold it; with scope player it is your…
- [Nodes › Game › Get Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/getvariable.md): Reads a named shared variable as a number — the read side of Set Variable, live on every player's screen.
- [Nodes › Game › Store Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storevalue.md): Saves a value on this device when a pulse arrives — a best score, the tallest tower, the level a player reached — so it survives a reload. It is never sent to other players and never written into…
- [Nodes › Game › Stored Value](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/storedvalue.md): Reads what a Store Value node saved on this device — the read side of a best score. Each player sees their own number.
- [Nodes › Game › Announce](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/announce.md): A big centred banner for a moment worth celebrating — "GOAL!", "Floor 3", "Ring 2 reached". On a desktop it sits over the game; in a headset it floats in front of the player.
- [Nodes › Game › Game Sound](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamesound.md): Plays one of the built-in game sounds when a pulse arrives — no audio files needed. Placed at a wired object (it pans and fades with distance), or everywhere when nothing is wired.
- [Nodes › Game › Effect Burst](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/effectburst.md): A short burst of particles — sparkles, confetti, smoke or sparks — at a wired object, or in front of the player when nothing is wired. Made for the moment a coin is collected, a ring is reached or…
- [Nodes › Game › Controller Buzz](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hapticpulse.md): Vibrates the VR controllers with a named pattern when a pulse arrives.
- [Nodes › Game › Game Music](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamemusic.md): Declares the scene's background music: one of seven built-in looping tracks, quiet under the game sounds, playing only while someone plays.
- [Nodes › Game › Game Setting](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamesetting.md): Adds one row to the game's Settings — the page in the game's pause menu, on the desktop and in VR — and outputs this player's value. Each player's choice is saved on their own device, for this…
- [Nodes › Game › Point Grab](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pointgrab.md): Decides whether players may pick objects up by pointing at them — the VR grip ray from a distance, or the desktop crosshair carry. While its enabled input reads off, only a hand that actually…
- [Nodes › Game › On Clap](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclap.md): Fires a pulse when a VR player brings both hands together and holds them there for a moment — a clap. It carries where the hands met, so a Spawn or an Effect Burst can make something right there.
- [Nodes › Game › Game Time](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gametime.md): The round clock: seconds since the round started, the same on every player's screen. It stops while the game is paused. It can also read the time left, the round number, or whether the game is…
- [Nodes › Game › Player Variable](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/peervariable.md): Reads a number kept per player — laps, touches, a personal score. Each player reads their own, or you can read one named player's, the team total, or the highest.
- [Nodes › Character › Character Controller](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/charcontroller.md): Sets how the player moves in Play: walking with gravity and a jump, or flying, at the speed you choose. There's nothing to trigger. The node works by being in the scene.
- [Nodes › Character › Move Input](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/moveinput.md): The player's own movement keys as numbers — the W/A/S/D axes — for driving things by hand.
- [Nodes › Character › Possess Object](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/possessnode.md): Puts the player in control of an object when a pulse arrives: a vehicle, a turret, a ball. A second input hands it back.
- [Nodes › Character › Camera Follow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/camerafollow.md): Makes your view follow an object from behind and above, as a third-person or chase view. Something else moves the object, and the camera just keeps up.
- [Nodes › Character › Move Speed](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/movespeed.md): Reads the player's movement speed, and sets a new one when a pulse arrives. Use it for sprint, mud or slow motion.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Screen](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudscreen.md): Shows, hides or toggles a whole HUD screen (a named layer of elements) each time a pulse arrives — open a pause menu, a map, a results screen.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Text](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudtext.md): Writes a number into a HUD text element through a format such as Gems: {v} — a score, a count, a readout.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Bar](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudbar.md): Drives a HUD bar element's fill from a number — health, fuel, progress.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Button](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudbutton.md): Fires a pulse when a HUD button is pressed - the on-screen counterpart of On Click.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Timer](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudtimer.md): Runs a countdown in a HUD Timer element from its duration, formatted like {v}s — it starts by itself or on a pulse.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD List](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudlist.md): Names a HUD List element and sets its title and how many rows it shows — an inventory, objectives, the players. The rows themselves are written into the list by a HUD Rows node, a Leaderboard, a…
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Rows](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudrows.md): Appends, replaces or clears rows in a HUD List element on a pulse — a log, a chat, a scoreboard feed.
- [Nodes › HUD › Leaderboard](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/leaderboard.md): Ranks the players by their own per-player variable (laps, score) into a HUD List element, highest or lowest first, top N rows.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Input](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudinput.md): Reads a HUD input element — what the player typed, picked, dragged or switched — as a value for the graph.
- [Nodes › HUD › HUD Set Input](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/hudset.md): Writes a value into a HUD input element when a pulse arrives — to prefill, clear or correct it: a Reset button that puts the volume back, a difficulty the host sets.
- [Nodes › Logic › Script](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/script.md): Write a small piece of code — the escape hatch when no built-in node fits. A Script node works two ways:
- [Nodes › Logic › Custom Node](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/customnode.md): Your own reusable node, designed in the app: named controls plus a per-frame script — shared with everyone in the session.
- [Nodes › Logic › Behaviour](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/behaviour.md): Game logic written as a small JavaScript file (params, replicated state, event handlers, kit calls) — run once on the authority peer, with a live node view of its events, state and knobs.
- [Nodes › Logic › Code link](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/coderef.md): Points at the module or kit file whose code runs part of this game — double-click (or Open code) to read it. It does nothing at runtime; it is how the Main graph shows where every rule lives.
- [Nodes › Logic › Math](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/math.md): Combines numbers with an arithmetic operation — two, or up to eight — or shapes one (sine, rounding, clamping…).
- [Nodes › Logic › Compare](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/compare.md): Compares two numbers and outputs true or false.
- [Nodes › Logic › Gate](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gate.md): Boolean logic — AND, OR, NOT, XOR — on two inputs, or up to eight.
- [Nodes › Logic › Map Range](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/maprange.md): Remaps a number from one range to another — the glue between free-range sources and bounded parameters.
- [Nodes › Logic › Select](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/select.md): Picks one of up to four values by an index: a, b, c or d.
- [Nodes › Logic › Latch](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/latch.md): Holds a boolean until told otherwise — set, reset and toggle pulses make it a memory bit. Every trigger in the graph is a short pulse; a Latch is how a pulse becomes something that stays: a door…
- [Nodes › Logic › Delay](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/delay.md): Passes a pulse on after a set number of seconds — the timing of a fuse, a door that closes later, a cooldown.
- [Nodes › Logic › Sequence](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/sequence.md): Fires its four outputs one after another from a single trigger — a step-by-step timeline: "light 1, then light 2 half a second later, then the door".
- [Nodes › Logic › Once](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/once.md): Lets exactly one pulse through until it is re-armed — a checkpoint, a pickup, a first-time event.
- [Nodes › Logic › Counter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/counter.md): Counts trigger pulses and outputs the running total.
- [Nodes › Logic › Loop](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/loop.md): Sweeps a number from one value to another over time, repeating — a ready-made animation ramp.
- [Nodes › Logic › Timer](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/timer.md): A delay line: outputs its input as it was a set number of seconds ago.
- [Nodes › Logic › Distance](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/distance.md): Measures the live distance between two things in the scene.
- [Nodes › Logic › Proximity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/proximity.md): True while two things are within a radius of each other — a distance sensor with the threshold built in.
- [Nodes › Logic › Look At](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/lookat.md): Keeps the connected object facing a target — another object or a fixed point — every frame.
- [Nodes › Logic › Set Color](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setcolor.md): Paints the connected object's material with a color, re-applied every frame.
- [Nodes › Logic › Visibility](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/visibility.md): Shows or hides the connected object based on a boolean.
- [Nodes › Logic › Set Shader Uniform](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setuniform.md): Writes one number inside an object's shader graph, so a trigger, a timer or a counter can drive how the material looks — a panel that heats up when you stand near it, a glow that pulses when…
- [Nodes › Triggers › On Click](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onclick.md): Fires a short pulse when its object is clicked — the bridge from user input into the graph.
- [Nodes › Triggers › On Grab](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/ongrab.md): Fires a pulse when a player picks up the connected object — a desktop carry in Play or Interact, or a VR grip in Interact.
- [Nodes › Triggers › Key Press](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/keypress.md): Fires a pulse while a keyboard key is pressed — the bridge from your keyboard into the graph.
- [Nodes › Triggers › On Hit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onhit.md): Fires a pulse when a hand or a player knocks the connected object — the trigger half of the knock.
- [Nodes › Triggers › On Rest](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onrest.md): Fires a pulse when a physics body has finished moving — the counterpart to On Impact, which fires when it starts.
- [Nodes › Triggers › Gamepad Button](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamepadbutton.md): Fires a pulse, or holds a level, while a gamepad button is pressed. It's the gamepad's counterpart of Key Press.
- [Nodes › Triggers › Gamepad Axis](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/gamepadaxis.md): A gamepad stick axis as a number between -1 and 1, with a dead zone of its own.
- [Nodes › Animation › Shake](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/shake.md): Jitters the connected object around its resting position — rumble, nervousness, impact feedback.
- [Nodes › Animation › Spin](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/spin.md): Rotates the connected object continuously around one axis.
- [Nodes › Animation › Rotate / Motor](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/rotor.md): Turns the connected object about its own local axis — and about its origin, so a wheel turns on its hub — at a set rpm. Paddles and scoops it turns carry water from Fluid emitters. On a dynamic…
- [Nodes › Animation › Float Along Flow](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/flowfloat.md): Carries the connected object along a Flow path — a leaf, a toy boat — at the path's speed, bobbing and turning with the current, looping at the end. Uses the nearest Flow path unless one is wired.
- [Nodes › Animation › Bounce](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bounce.md): Bounces the connected object up and down off its resting height, like a dribbled ball.
- [Nodes › Animation › Orbit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/orbit.md): Circles the connected object around its resting position on the horizontal plane.
- [Nodes › Animation › Path Patrol](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pathpatrol.md): Walks the connected object along a series of waypoints you click into the scene, facing along the path.
- [Nodes › Animation › Follow Path](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/followpath.md): Moves the connected object along a smooth path — a drawn Spline, a Flow path or its own waypoints — at a speed, looping, ping-ponging or once, facing along it and leaning into the turns. An offset…
- [Nodes › Animation › Wander](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/wander.md): Drifts the connected object around a smooth, never-repeating target inside an area object (a water volume, a room) or a box around where it was placed — fish, birds, fireflies, idle drones.
- [Nodes › Animation › Orient to Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/orientvelocity.md): Turns the connected object to face the way it is moving, smoothly, leaning into turns — put it after Wander, Orbit or any mover so it looks where it goes.
- [Nodes › Animation › Body Wave](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bodywave.md): Bends the connected object with a wave travelling along its body — a swimming fish, a snake, a flag, a tail — stronger and faster the faster it moves, curving into turns. A shader effect: physics…
- [Nodes › Animation › Animation Finished](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animfinished.md): Pulses when a once clip reaches its end — the other half of Play Animation, so a movement can hand off to whatever comes next.
- [Nodes › Animation › Animation Marker](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animmarker.md): Pulses as the playhead crosses a named marker inside a clip — so a footstep, a puff of dust or a latch click can sit at an exact frame of a movement instead of only at its end.
- [Nodes › Animation › Animation State](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/animstate.md): Reads what a clip is doing, as a number — the readable half of Animation Finished. Use it to drive something continuously instead of only handing off at the end.
- [Nodes › Animation › Play Animation](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/playanim.md): Plays a keyframed clip on an object — the bridge from an event into an authored animation. Wire an On Click to it and a door opens for everybody who sees it clicked.
- [Nodes › Animation › Play Sequence](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/playseq.md): Plays, stops, toggles or restarts a Timeline sequence (camera shots, clips, audio, events) for every player when a pulse arrives. New in 1.39; find it in the palette under Animation.
- [Nodes › Animation › On Sequence Event](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onseqevent.md): Fires a pulse when a running Timeline sequence passes a named event item, or reaches its end (end). New in 1.39; find it in the palette under Animation.
- [Nodes › Physics › On Impact](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onimpact.md): Fires a pulse when, in a physics simulation, the connected object hits something — from any side, or only when it lands (the From option).
- [Nodes › Physics › On Enter](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onenter.md): Fires a pulse when something enters a trigger volume — the checkpoint, doorway and pressure-plate node.
- [Nodes › Physics › On Exit](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/onexit.md): Fires a pulse when something leaves a trigger volume — the other half of On Enter.
- [Nodes › Physics › Mass](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/mass.md): Gives the connected object weight for the physics simulation — objects with a Mass fall and collide.
- [Nodes › Physics › Bounciness](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/bounciness.md): Sets how much the connected object rebounds in the physics simulation (restitution).
- [Nodes › Physics › Friction](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/friction.md): Sets how much the connected object grips surfaces in the physics simulation.
- [Nodes › Physics › Angular Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/angularvelocity.md): Gives the connected object a constant spin under physics — a rolling barrel, a spinning hazard, a rotating platform other objects can stand on.
- [Nodes › Physics › Collider](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/collider.md): Overrides the collision shape (see Colliders) the physics simulation uses for the connected object — the flow equivalent of the Inspector's Physics ▸ Collider pick, and it wins over it.
- [Nodes › Physics › Motor](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/motor.md): Drives every hinge joint attached to the connected object — the flow way to make wheels turn, turntables spin and doors swing under power.
- [Nodes › Physics › Impulse](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/impulse.md): Pushes or spins a physics body when an event fires — a jump, a kick, a cannon, a nudge.
- [Nodes › Physics › Set Velocity](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/setvelocity.md): Sets a physics body's speed outright — to launch it at an exact velocity, to hold it at a constant one, or to stop it dead.
- [Nodes › Physics › Joint](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/joint.md): Attaches two objects to each other when an event fires — a hinge, or a rigid weld.
- [Nodes › Effects › Pulse](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/pulse.md): Throbs the connected object's scale in and out around its resting size.
- [Nodes › Effects › Blink](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/blink.md): Flashes the connected object on and off at a steady rate.
- [Nodes › Effects › Sound](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/sound.md): Plays an audio file from the connected object — positional 3D sound that everyone hears.
- [Nodes › Effects › Particles](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/particle.md): Emits a particle effect from the connected object — the flow-graph version of the Particle Effects feature, so you can drive emission, colour and bursts from other nodes.
- [Nodes › Effects › Jiggle](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/jiggle.md): Makes the connected object jiggle — it lags behind when moved, wobbles like jelly on impact and sways in the wind; skinned models swing their bone chains (tails, hair, antennae).
- [Nodes › Music › Device Param](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/deviceparam.md): Writes a number into one parameter of the connected audio device every frame - an LFO on a cutoff, a fader on a level.
- [Nodes › Music › Device Level](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/devicelevel.md): The live output level of the connected audio device (or a wired one) as a number - a meter you can drive anything with.
- [Nodes › Music › Transport](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/transportbeat.md): The shared music transport as a number - beat, bar, phase, bpm or playing - identical on every peer.
- [Nodes › Music › Note Trigger](https://docs.theprototype.app/nodes/notetrigger.md): Plays a note on the connected audio device when a pulse arrives - a drum pad, a sampler pad, a synth key.

- [Behaviours](https://docs.theprototype.app/behaviours.md): Some game logic is easier to write than to wire: a loop over waves, a rule with three exceptions, a timer that calls itself. A behaviour is that logic as one small JavaScript file inside a node —…

## Extending

- [Modules](https://docs.theprototype.app/modules.md): Modules plug playable content into the app — instruments, mini-games, generators, custom nodes and tools — and everything they do replicates to every connected peer.
- [Module SDK](https://docs.theprototype.app/module-sdk.md): Modules plug playable content into theprototype.app: instruments, game prototypes, generators, custom nodes and tools. A module registers itself through one register(api) call and everything it…
- [Module Packages](https://docs.theprototype.app/module-package.md): The format the Modules manager installs (zip upload or URL) and exports ("Download as example"). One folder or zip root per module.
- [UI kit for modules](https://docs.theprototype.app/ui-kit.md): theprototype.app draws its windows, settings and inspector from one small set of parts and one set of design tokens. Build your module's UI from the same parts and it looks native, follows the…
